title: Counterattack
statementMd:
Long long ago, the universe existed as a high-dimensional space. Planets are neatly arranged here. Interstellar conflicts occur frequently, yet counterattacks are not allowed.

In an $n$-dimensional space, the coordinate of the $i$-th dimension is an integer within the range $[1, a_i]$. The set of all lattice points is defined as:

$$ \{(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n) \mid 1 \le x_i \le a_i,\ x_i \in \mathbb{Z}\}. $$

Initially, all points satisfying $x_i \le b_i$ for every $i$ are colored black (every coordinate is no larger than the corresponding threshold $b_i$), and all other points are white.

Alice and Bob take turns to perform operations, and Alice moves first. In each turn, the current player must select a white point $P = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)$. After the selection, all points $Q = (y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)$ satisfying $y_i \ge x_i$ for every $i$ will be colored black. A player loses if they cannot choose any white point to operate on.

Both players adopt optimal strategies. For each test case, determine whether Alice has a winning strategy.

## Input

The first line contains an integer $T$ $(1 \le T \le 2\times 10^5)$, representing the number of test cases.

For each test case:

The first line contains an integer $n$ $(1\le n \le 2\times 10^5)$.

The second line contains $n$ integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ $(1 \le a_i \le 10^9)$.

The third line contains $n$ integers $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ $(1 \le b_i \le a_i \le 10^9)$.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $2\times 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output one line. Print `Yes` if Alice has a winning strategy, otherwise print `No`. The answer is case-insensitive.
